info.name: Feats
info.description: Origin and General Feats from Steinhardt’s Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024).

element.name: Curious
element.source: Steinhardt’s Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: Origin Feat
You gain the following benefits.

Learn. Whenever you make an ability check using a skill you are not proficient in, you can become proficient in that skill until you finish a Long Rest. Once you use this benefit, you can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest.
Observe. Immediately after you roll Initiative, you can choose one creature you can see in the same combat. You learn any of the creature’s Resistances and Vulnerabilities.

sheet.description: Whenever you make an ability check using a skill you are not proficient in, you can become proficient in that skill until you finish a Long Rest. Immediately after you roll Initiative, you can choose one creature you can see in the same combat and learn any of its Resistances and Vulnerabilities.

element.name: Faithful
element.source: Steinhardt’s Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: Origin Feat
You gain the following benefits.

Divine Clarity. If you fail a saving throw against the Charmed or Frightened condition, you can choose to succeed instead. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.
Trial of Faith. Whenever you roll a 1 on a D20 Test, you gain Heroic Inspiration.

sheet.description: If you fail a saving throw against the Charmed or Frightened condition, you can choose to succeed instead. Whenever you roll a 1 on a D20 Test, you gain Heroic Inspiration.

element.name: Grizzled
element.source: Steinhardt’s Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: Origin Feat
You gain the following benefits.
Overcome. Whenever you make a saving throw against the Frightened condition, you gain a bonus to the saving throw equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
Survive. You require half as much food and water to survive, and you have Advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks made to forage for food and water.
Withstand. Whenever you become Bloodied, you gain Heroic Inspiration.

sheet.description: Whenever you make a saving throw against the Frightened condition, you gain a +{{proficiency}} bonus to the saving throw. You require half as much food and water to survive, and have Advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks made to forage for food and water. Whenever you become Bloodied, you gain Heroic Inspiration.

element.name: Worthless
element.source: Steinhardt’s Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: Origin Feat (Prerequisite: Level below 4)
You gain the following benefits.

Worthless. When you gain this Origin Feat, reduce your highest ability score (your choice if they are equal) until the sum of your six ability scores is equal to or lower than 72. Then, reduce each ability score by 1.

From the Ashes. When you reach character level 4, and again at character levels 8, 12, 16, and 19, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. You can't increase an ability score above 18 using this benefit.

sheet.description: When you gain this feat, manually reduce your highest ability score until the sum of your six ability scores is 72 or lower (before the -1 penalty applied to all scores). At levels 4, 8, 12, 16, and 19, you can increase one ability score by 2, or two ability scores by 1 (to a maximum of 18 using this benefit).

element.name: Brutalizer
element.source: Steinhardt’s Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: General Feat (Prerequisite: Level 4+, Strength 16+)
You master a reckless approach that maximizes your offensive capabilities. You gain the following benefits.
Ability Score Increase. Increase your Strength or Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
Brutal Weaponry. You can wield a weapon with the Two-Handed property in one hand, as long as your other hand is empty or wielding a one-handed weapon.
Killing Streak. When you reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points, your next attack roll before the end of your next turn has Advantage.

sheet.description: You can wield a weapon with the Two-Handed property in one hand, as long as your other hand is empty or wielding a one-handed weapon. When you reduce a creature to 0 HP, your next attack roll before the end of your next turn has Advantage.

element.name: Cannoneer
element.source: Steinhardt’s Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: General Feat (Prerequisite: Level 8+, Strength 18+)
The best defense is a good offense, and the best offense is a cannon; you gain the following benefits.
Ability Score Increase. Increase your Strength score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

Cannon Proficiency. You gain proficiency with Cannons, and you can reload a Cannon as a Bonus Action instead of an action. You can take this Bonus Action only if you haven’t moved during your turn, and after you take the Bonus Action, your Speed is 0 until the end of your turn. Starting at character level 11, this doesn’t reduce your Speed, and when you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with reloading the Cannon. When you reach character level 20, you can ignore the Artillery property of Cannons.
Siege. Your attacks with Cannons deal double damage to objects and structures.
Strong Back. The weight of Cannons and Cannonballs count as half for you.

sheet.description: You can reload a Cannon as a Bonus Action if you haven’t moved during your turn (your Speed becomes 0 until the end of your turn). Your attacks with Cannons deal double damage to objects and structures, and the weight of Cannons and Cannonballs count as half for you.

You can reload a Cannon as a Bonus Action if you haven’t moved during your turn. You can replace one attack of your Attack action with reloading a Cannon. Your attacks with Cannons deal double damage to objects and structures, and the weight of Cannons and Cannonballs count as half for you.

You can reload a Cannon as a Bonus Action if you haven’t moved during your turn. You can replace one attack of your Attack action with reloading a Cannon. You ignore the Artillery property of Cannons. Your attacks with Cannons deal double damage to objects and structures, and the weight of Cannons and Cannonballs count as half for you.

element.name: Cosmos Touched
element.source: Steinhardt’s Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: General Feat (Prerequisite: Level 4+)
You gain the following benefits.
Ability Score Increase. Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

Cosmos Magic. Choose one level 1 spell from the Abjuration or Transmutation school of magic. You always have that spell and the Alter Self spell prepared. You can cast each of these spells without a spell slot. Once you cast either spell in this way, you can't cast that spell in this way again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast these spells using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. The spells' spellcasting ability is the ability increased by this feat.

element.name: Intelligence
element.source: Steinhardt’s Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: Increase your Intelligence by 1, to a maximum of 20.

sheet.description: You can cast each of this feat’s spells without a spell slot once per Long Rest. You can also cast these spells using spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Your spellcasting ability for these spells is Intelligence.

element.name: Focused Hunter
element.source: Steinhardt’s Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: General Feat (Prerequisite: Level 4+)
During hunts, you are capable of bursts of focus when you need them most. You gain the following benefits:
Ability Score Increase. Increase your Strength or Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

Improved Focus. You gain 1 Adrenaline Point (adding to your existing Adrenaline Points if you already have Adrenaline Points), and learn one new Adrenaline Art, choosing from Weapon Parry, Dodge Step, or any of the Jaeger’s Additional Adrenaline Arts. You regain all expended Adrenaline Points when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

element.name: Focused Hunter
element.source: Steinhardt’s Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: You don't have Adrenaline Points

sheet.description: You gain 1 Adrenaline Point and learn one Adrenaline Art.

element.name: Marksman
element.source: Steinhardt’s Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: General Feat (Prerequisite: Level 4+)
You know your firearms inside and out and are a master at handling them. You gain the following benefits.
Ability Score Increase. Increase your Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

Fast Hands. You can reload weapons with the Barrel property as a Bonus Action even if they do not possess the Light property. If a weapon possesses both the Barrel and Light properties, you can ignore the Barrel property.

Steady Aim. Being within 5 feet of an enemy doesn't impose Disadvantage on your ranged attack rolls, nor do you have Disadvantage on ranged attacks against creatures with the Prone condition within 30 feet of you.

sheet.description: You can reload weapons with the Barrel property as a Bonus Action even if they lack the Light property. If a weapon has both Barrel and Light, you ignore the Barrel property. Being within 5ft. of an enemy doesn't impose Disadvantage on your ranged attack rolls, and you don't have Disadvantage on ranged attacks against Prone creatures within 30ft. of you.

element.name: Osteomantic Adept
element.source: Steinhardt’s Guide to the Eldritch Hunt (2024)

description.p: General Feat (Prerequisite: Level 4+)
You gain the following benefits.
Ability Score Increase. Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

Empowered Osteomancy. When you cast an Osteomancy* spell of level 1 or higher, you can sacrifice your life force to empower it, increasing the level this spell is cast at by one. You then roll a number of d6s equal to half the original spell's level (rounded up, minimum of 1) and take Necrotic damage equal to the number rolled, which can’t be reduced or prevented in any way.
The first time you use this benefit after you finish a Long Rest, it doesn’t damage you.

p.i: *Osteomancy Spells: Amputate, Arm Cannon, Aspect of Death, Bone Claws, Bone Cocoon, Bone Shield, Boneyard, Brittle Bone Throw, Calcified Memories, Chisel Skull, Displacing Maw, Dread Scarecrow, Forest of Dread, Fractured Shell, Maiden of Bones, Marrow Transfer, Osseous Cage, Osseous Impalement, Osteophagia, Phalangeal Shot, Rolling Bones, Rubber Bones, Rupturing Curse, Skeletal Tail, Wall of Bones.

sheet.description: When you cast an Osteomancy spell of level 1+, you can cast it at one level higher by rolling d6s equal to half the original spell's level (rounded up, min 1) and taking unavoidable Necrotic damage equal to the roll. The first time you use this benefit after a Long Rest, it doesn’t damage you.
